person: Lan Tran is a 41-year-old pharmacy technician who works rotating shifts and handles the family's paperwork on her phone. Her mother, Thu, is 67 and lives with her. Thu retires from her laundry job at the end of this month and never took Medicare Part B. Lan manages Thu's Medicare with her permission, and also answers questions from Thu's husband, Bao, who has retiree coverage from his old job. Lan reads official letters slowly in English and worries about hidden fees, because she once paid a helper for nothing.
stated_up_front: Hello, my mother Thu stops work on October 30 and I need to do her Medicare Part B. A man said to take COBRA, I am not sure. Please tell me if anything costs money.

facts.about: Day Thu's work health coverage ends
Thu's employer and how long she has had the plan
facts.truth: Bayview Hospital Laundry; she has been on its group health plan from her own job since 2011
She is 67. She has Medicare Part A only and never signed up for Part B.

facts.about: Who is on Thu's work plan
facts.truth: Thu and her son Tuan, 24, who is Lan's brother and is not on Medicare
Bao Le, 70, Thu's husband, has retiree coverage from his old job at a bakery supply company since February 2025. He has no Part B and asks if he should sign up too.
A broker, Mr. Kevin Doyle, emailed that Thu should take COBRA and wait on Part B. The COBRA notice says $812 a month.
An email offers to file Medicare forms for $299. Lan does not want to pay.

facts.about: Coverage Lan wants kept until new coverage starts
facts.truth: Thu's, Tuan's and Bao's coverage should stay as it is. Nothing should be cancelled yet.
Lan is Thu's daughter and helps with her permission, using Thu's accounts on Lan's phone

unknowns: Whether Bao's retiree coverage lets him sign up for Part B now
What the form CMS-L564 is and who must fill it
How many months Thu has to sign up, and whether there is a penalty
Whether COBRA keeps Thu's Part B sign-up time open
